name: median3x3
description: A streaming 3x3 median filter (salt-and-pepper denoise) using an odd-even transposition sorting network; compares only, no multiplier.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Synthesizable streaming 3x3 median filter for salt-and-pepper (impulse) denoise. One 8-bit pixel per cycle enters in raster order; in_sof pulses on the first pixel of a frame and the same framing is reproduced on out_valid/out_pix/out_sof, so the output is same-size (one output pixel per input pixel, zero-padded border) and a valid input to the next filter. Two line buffers (lambdalib la_spram BRAM, depth IMGW) plus a 2-stage alignment pipeline absorb the synchronous-read latency and align three window rows; a 3-column shift register forms the 3x3 window. The nine window pixels feed an odd-even transposition sorting network (36 compare-swaps) and the middle element (median of 9) is output. It shares an identical streaming interface with sobel3x3 and conv2d so the three filters cascade directly.
key_decisions: Median computed with a sorting network of compare-swap cells (odd-even transposition / Batcher style), so the datapath is compares only with 0 DSP.
Compare-swap network built with generate (one combinational compare-swap unit per element) rather than a single large unrolled procedural loop.
Two line buffers implemented with lambdalib la_spram (BRAM), depth IMGW, read-first row delay, chained with a 2-stage alignment pipeline to absorb 1-cycle synchronous-read latency.
Same-size output with zero-padded borders (out-of-frame neighbors forced to zero) so image geometry is preserved across a cascade.
Shared pixel-stream interface (clk/rst/in_valid/in_sof/in_pix -> out_valid/out_sof/out_pix) common to sobel3x3, median3x3, and conv2d so filters chain directly.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: J. Tukey, Exploratory Data Analysis, Addison-Wesley, 1977 (running median; median filtering for impulse noise).
K. E. Batcher, 'Sorting networks and their applications,' AFIPS Spring Joint Computer Conference, 1968 (sorting-network median, odd-even transposition).
Line-buffer streaming image-filter architecture (sliding-window line buffers).
